sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 35 (check 34) and Internal Quality Checks row 35 (no internal annotation for this row)
evidence: Every interactive, time-varying and viewport promise in the brief has a step that tells the judge to click, type, press a key, wait or resize. A still first paint cannot pass any of them. Live updates: functional live_updates_keep_my_work (functional/judge.toml:239-242) sets up a second context with a scrolled thread, an open reply box and a half-typed draft. It then needs four remote changes to appear 'without reloading, within about ten seconds' while the draft, the box and the scroll position are kept. wall_added_live (:91-92) needs M-13 to vanish from Sian's open page within about ten seconds with no reload. unread_and_new_messages_line (:211-215) checks counts in two Dev contexts within about ten seconds. Keyboard and transient UI: polish enter_sends (Shift+Enter then Enter), escape_closes (Escape on the edit box and the reply box, then a reload), delete_confirm (decline and confirm) and wall_mentions_and_links Part B (type '@', pick a suggestion). Waits: link_highlight requires the highlight to persist about ten seconds later, and refusal_in_place waits about ten seconds to rule out a toast. Viewport: polish transcript_print sets 390x844 and measures documentElement.scrollWidth. The visual prompt (visual/prompt.md:153) says to resize to 1440x900 and to 390x844 for phone_chambers. Multi-context setup is explained in app_context.md:24. The v2 hosted Oracle details show judges really did this on the previous bytes: the 10-second wait in refusal_in_place, scrollWidth=390 at 390x844 in phone_chambers, and two-context waits in wall_added_live, unread and live_updates. Risk=true because no full configured judge run exists for these v3 bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says so). The scripted golden in functional.cjs (hash verified, e.g. lines 659-700) is not judge behaviour, so whether the judge performs the v3 waits and resizes within the 550 s per-criterion cap is unmeasured. Minor note, outside this row's scope: the v2 polish phone_matter scrollWidth check on the thread was replaced. The brief's 'whole app at 390 px with no sideways scroll' is now measured strictly only on the transcript; the thread at 390 is judged visually in phone_chambers. Coverage rows should confirm that this is enough.
